entry.title: Re: IMPORT_UNEXPECTED_END_OF_DATA at start of update function module
entry.content:
Probably the type of the parameter in the function module is not the same type as the argument passed to this parameter.

For instance, the parameter type could be table instead of structure.

Because they are of different types, there's a failure in the internal call of IMPORT used by the kernel to pass the arguments of update function modules called in update task.

Sandra

Hello, SAP Community!

If you've been following SAP platform story, you already know about SAP Business AI Platform. It is SAP’s enterprise AI foundation to build, contextualize, and govern every application and workflow.

This blog is your guide to the updated SAP Business AI Platform Adoption Framework and how to get started with your own platform Maturity Assessment, available through SAP Discovery Center. It's perfectly timed to help you prepare for SAP TechEd. 

Where Do You Stand? The Platform Maturity Assessment on SAP Discovery Center

 

One of the most practical things you can do as you evaluate your next step in enterprise AI is to take the Platform Maturity Assessment on SAP Discovery Center. This is a free, guided self-assessment that takes you through key dimensions of platform adoption and gives you:

  • A baseline maturity score for your organization
  • A clear snapshot of your current state across strategy, architecture, adoption, and more
  • Identified gaps and prioritized recommendations
  • The ability to model what a jump to the next maturity level would require

The Five Maturity Levels

Here's how they map to the journey most organizations are on:

 

 

The assessment asks you about strategy (how familiar is your organization with SAP's platform direction, who drives platform strategy, how ROI is measured), architecture, tooling adoption, governance, and your AI readiness. It's brief enough to complete in one sitting, but rich enough to give you genuinely useful output. It's structured around the SAP Business AI Platform pillars, making it directly relevant to your organization's enterprise AI.

  • Strategy: How your organization approaches enterprise AI adoption
  • Build - Develop: Your current state with development tools and frameworks
  • Build - Integrate: Integration maturity across your landscape
  • Contextualize and Reason - Data and Analytics: How you manage and activate business data
  • Contextualize and Reason - AI Models: AI model readiness and use
  • Govern: Your approach to AI governance, security, and compliance

If you're scaling AI across specific verticals like finance, HR, supply chain, or procurement, the LoB-specific AI Maturity Assessments introduced at SAP Sapphire 2026 are also available on SAP Discovery Center. These are designed for line-of-business teams asking, "What does AI adoption look like in my function?" and are aligned with the Autonomous Enterprise journey.

You can save multiple assessments, compare them over time, and collaborate with your team through shared editing and comment threads. It's designed to be a living tool, not a one-time snapshot. The assessment is directly aligned with the journey to the Autonomous Enterprise.

And if you want to go a step further, there's a new AI-Assisted Solution Blueprint Proposal feature in beta on SAP Discovery Center right now. It takes your business requirements and maps them to the right combination of SAP AI solutions automatically. Read all about it in my colleague @KatrinVonAhsen’s blog AI-Assisted Solution Blueprint Proposal Feature on SAP Discovery Center. You can also visit SAP Customer Influence & Adoption page and follow the registration instructions to sign up for the beta program. 

 

Join Us at SAP TechEd 2026

Closing Thoughts

 

Whether you're building applications, integrating systems, automating processes, or exploring intelligent agents, SAP TechEd 2026 is the place to learn what's possible with SAP Business AI Platform and how to accelerate your organization’s AI journey.

entry.title: Re: Non-Mandatory Item Retraining Periods - SF Learning
entry.content:
Using two Curricula with the same Items in it for First Aid might be a solution for you.  If for instance if you are in Australia, then the Nationally Recognised course is "Provide First Aid" and is made up of the following nationally recognised units of competency:

  • - HLTAID011 Provide First Aid
  • - HLTAID010 Provide basic emergency life support
  • - HLTAID009 Provide cardiopulmonary resuscitation

So, if you created the following curricula:  CUR- Provide First Aid- REQUIRED

  • - HLTAID011 Provide First Aid
  • - HLTAID010 Provide basic emergency life support
  • - HLTAID009 Provide cardiopulmonary resuscitation

With the Initial Period set at "14 days", the Retraining Period of "1,095 days", and the Assignment Type as "Required" (aka Required = Yes).

Then assigned this curriculum by role specific Assignment Profile/s (or Manually) it would manage those employees that require this training for their roles. Showing them over due to complete the training and its expiry.

And a Second Curricula with all the same Items:  CUR- Provide First Aid- OPTIONAL

  • - HLTAID011 Provide First Aid
  • - HLTAID010 Provide basic emergency life support

entry.title: Re: Building Your First Data Product in SAP Datasphere: Step-by-Step Practical Guide
entry.content:
Hi @igdulia ,

Thank you for your detailed question and for highlighting this important distinction.

In my example, I am using an SAP HANA Database (Disk and In-Memory) Space, not an SAP HANA Data Lake Files Space.

The guide focuses on creating a Marketplace Data Product in SAP Datasphere using the Data Sharing Cockpit.

For your scenario, I would recommend the following architecture:

1. Data Replication

Replicate the master data from SAP BW into local tables in an SAP HANA Database Space, including the Attribute and Text tables.

2. Dimension Modeling

Create Graphical Views to combine the relevant master data attributes and texts.

Set the appropriate semantic usage (Dimension), define the necessary keys and associations, and deploy the views. For multilingual texts, you can also consider separate Text entities with the corresponding associations.

3. SAP Analytics Cloud Consumption

Reuse these Dimensions in an Analytic Model by associating them with the relevant Fact entities.

The Analytic Model can then be consumed in SAP Analytics Cloud through a live connection.

One important distinction is that standalone Dimension Views are generally not consumed directly as live analytical models in SAC. They are typically reused within an Analytic Model.

4. Data Product Creation

If your requirement is to create a Marketplace Data Product within SAP Datasphere, you can reuse the same deployed Graphical Views.

Navigate to:

Data Sharing Cockpit → My Data Products → Create Data Product

  • Create a Data Product called BW Master Data.

  • Select your SAP HANA Database Space as the Artifact Space.

  • Add your deployed Graphical Views as Product Artifacts.

  • Configure the appropriate context and delivery mode.

  • Save and list the Data Product.

This allows multiple modeled Dimensions, such as Customer, Material, and Cost Center, to be included as artifacts in one Data Product.

5. When Would You Need an SAP HANA Data Lake Files Space?

This becomes relevant if you want to publish a custom Data Product for SAP Business Data Cloud using Delta Sharing.

In that case, the architecture is different because the supported artifacts are Local Tables (File), not Graphical Views.

You could follow this approach:

SAP BW → HANA Database Space → Graphical Views → Materialized Local Tables → HANA Data Lake Files Space → Local Tables (File) → BDC Data Product

The modeled results would need to be materialized and made available as Local Tables (File) in the Data Lake Files Space, for example through an appropriate sharing and transformation flow process.

Alternatively, if the BW data already resides in a File Space, you can use Spark Transformation Flows to prepare the output tables and share them with a HANA Database Space for analytical modeling.

My Recommendation

For your specific scenario, where the primary goal is to reuse business Dimensions in SAC while also publishing them as part of a Data Product, I would start with an SAP HANA Database Space.

You can maintain your business logic and semantic modeling in one place and reuse the deployed Views for the Marketplace Data Product.

Only introduce the HANA Data Lake Files layer if your requirement specifically includes publishing a Delta Share Data Product through SAP Business Data Cloud.

I hope this clarifies the difference between the two approaches and helps with your architecture decision.

Thank you again for raising this point. I will also make the Space type distinction clearer in the guide.

Sorry for answering in English, my German is not good enough for this one. I followed it in the code of an S/4HANA 2023 system, and the short version is: on S/4HANA the TCP0I entry is never read.

The Form Builder asks function module NLS_WORD_ENABLE (function group S_NLS_BIDI) if it should open Word. Its first lines are IF cl_cos_utilities=>is_s4h( ). ex_oi_editor = 'X'. EXIT. ENDIF. So on S/4HANA it answers "Word" before it looks at TCP0I. RSCPSETEDITOR even has a message for it, RIN 047: "MS Word Editor cannot be disabled for S4H installations." The two options you tried don't help either. On the settings screen (program SAPLSTXB, screen 2033), "Text Edit Control" and "Table Control Editor" are in the group "ABAP Editor". They set g_settings-set_edit, which is the editor for program lines, not for texts.

What skips Word is the other group on the same screen, "Inplace Editor", checkbox "Line Editor" (Zeileneditor, field SSFSCREEN-SET_ED_LE):

  • Inline editor: in FORM CREATE_EDITOR_CONTROL (include LSTXBF09), g_settings-set_line_edit = 'X' is checked before the Word check, and you get a line editor in an ALV grid.
  • Full screen text editor: EDIT_TEXT is called with line_editor = g_settings-set_line_edit, and FULL_SCREEN_NEW then sets pc_editor to false, so NLS_WORD_ENABLE is not called there either.

It's the old line editor, not as comfortable as Word, but it's plain ITF and no Word.

entry.title: iFlow Transport with Git and CI/CD – Setting Externalized Parameters with Automation Pilot
entry.content:
Introduction

Here are two recent updates around Cloud Integration:

  • July 2026: Cloud Integration can push iFlows to a Git repository and pull them from it.
  • September 2026: SAP Automation Pilot introduced the SAP Integration Suite (is-sapcp) catalog. It manages the lifecycle of iFlows, externalized parameters and the Partner Directory.

In addition, SAP Continuous Integration and Delivery (CI/CD) provides the SAP Integration Suite Artifacts 2.0 job. It takes an iFlow from a Git repository, uploads it to a target tenant and deploys it.

A possible next step would be to combine them: push an iFlow to Git, transport it to the target tenant with CI/CD, and then set the externalized parameters for that environment with Automation Pilot.

So I tried it. In this blog post, I will show how I connected these services and which gaps I had to bridge.

Note: I tested this on a BTP trial account. It is not a production-proven procedure.

Architecture

Figure: Overall architecture

  1. Develop the iFlow in the Dev tenant and push it to GitHub.
  2. Run the CI/CD job. It uploads the iFlow to the target tenant and deploys it.
  3. When the job succeeds, Alert Notification triggers an Automation Pilot command. The command sets the externalized parameters for the target environment and deploys them.

CI/CD deploys the iFlow, and Automation Pilot deploys only the externalized parameters.

Bridging the gaps

Gap 1: Repository structure

When Cloud Integration pushes an iFlow, it creates a folder named after the iFlow ID, so one repository can hold several iFlows. The CI/CD job, however, expects the content of one iFlow at the repository root.

# Pushed by Cloud Integration   # Expected by CI/CD
Test_Flow/                       META-INF/
├── META-INF/                    src/
├── src/                         metainfo.prop
└── metainfo.prop

As-is, the Upload stage fails with Integration flow project must contain a manifest file. The fix is one additional command in the Upload stage (Additional Commands > Run First in Stage). It zips the iFlow folder into the package.zip that the stage uploads:

python3 -c "import shutil; shutil.make_archive('package','zip','<iFlow ID>')"

Figure: Additional command in the Upload stage

Gap 2: Passing externalized parameters to Automation Pilot

The Automation Pilot command BulkPromoteIFlowToEnvironment takes the iFlow ID (iflowId) and the externalized parameters to set in the target environment (iflowParameters). The CI/CD Build Notification can carry such values in its Custom Tag:

Figure: Custom tag in the Build Notification settings

When Alert Notification triggers Automation Pilot, though, the whole event goes to the command as one input. The following JSON is the event (abbreviated). The custom tag is nested inside it as a JSON string:

{
  "eventType": "build.end",
  "subject": "Build has finished with 'SUCCESS'",
  "tags": {
    "cicd:custom": "{\"iflowId\": \"Test_Flow\", \"iflowParameters\": [{\"key\":\"header1\",\"value\":\"bulk\"}]}",
    "cicd:issuer": "SAP Continuous Integration and Delivery",
    "cicd:stage": "Integration Flow Result",
    ...
  },
  "resource": { "resourceType": "SAP Integration Suite Artifacts", ... },
  ...
}

So I created a small wrapper command, PromoteIFlowFromAnsEvent, with the help of SAP Automation Pilot Agent Skills. It receives the whole event as its payload input and runs two steps:

  1. customTag reads the cicd:custom tag from the event. If the tag has no iflowId, the command stops with an error message.
  2. promote calls BulkPromoteIFlowToEnvironment. It takes iflowId and iflowParameters from the custom tag (see the red boxes in the figure below), and the connection details of the target tenant from the command's input.

Figure: The promote step of the wrapper command

You can import the command from GitHub: https://github.com/miyasuta/automation-pilot-cicd-iflow

Configuration

Prerequisites:

  • A GitHub repository and a personal access token (PAT)
  • The following services in your subaccount:
    • SAP Integration Suite
    • SAP Continuous Integration and Delivery
    • SAP Alert Notification service
    • SAP Automation Pilot

1. Cloud Integration

Connect the repository and push the iFlow. See Integrating with GitHub and this blog post.

2. CI/CD

Set up an Integration Suite Artifacts 2.0 job as described in the documentation. Notes:

  • Create the integration package in the target tenant beforehand. CI/CD does not create it.
  • For Design Time Authentication, use a service key of SAP Process Integration Runtime (plan api) in the target subaccount.
  • Additional settings for this scenario:
    • Upload > Additional Commands > Run First in Stage: Enter the zip command (Gap 1)
    • Build Notification: Turn on the notification, and enter the Alert Notification service key and the custom tag (Gap 2)

3. Automation Pilot

This step assumes that the wrapper command (Gap 2) already exists in your Automation Pilot tenant.

  1. Create an Input with the target tenant's credentials (clientId, clientSecret, tokenUrl, apiHost) from a service key of SAP Process Integration Runtime (plan api).
  2. In Executions, click Build Event Trigger. Select the command and the input. On the Mapping tab, map the event to payload. Copy the event trigger URL.

Figure: Build Event Trigger, General tab

Figure: Build Event Trigger, Mapping tab

The SAP Process Integration Runtime (plan api) service instances used by CI/CD and Automation Pilot have the following roles:

RoleCI/CDAutomation Pilot
WorkspacePackagesEdit✓✓
WorkspaceArtifactsDeploy✓✓
MonitoringDataRead✓✓
WorkspacePackagesConfigure ✓

Automation Pilot additionally needs WorkspacePackagesConfigure to update the externalized parameters.

4. Alert Notification

In Alert Notification, configure the following so that a successful CI/CD build triggers the Automation Pilot command:

  • Action: Create an action that calls the event trigger URL. Enter the username and password for the event trigger.
  • Conditions: Create two conditions so that only successful builds trigger the command: eventType equals build.end, and subject contains SUCCESS. For details of the event, see the event reference.
  • Subscription: Create a subscription that combines the action and both conditions.

Result

I ran the CI/CD job, and it finished successfully:

Figure: Successful CI/CD build

Alert Notification triggered the command:

Figure: Command execution in Automation Pilot

The externalized parameter has the value from the custom tag:

Figure: Externalized parameter set in the target tenant

Considerations

  • Single iFlows only. Both the Git integration and the CI/CD job handle individual iFlows. Scripts, value mappings and other artifacts in the package are not transported. If the iFlow depends on them, import the package to the target first.
  • One CI/CD job per iFlow and target environment. The number of jobs grows with the number of iFlows and environments. This setup can be an option for two-tier landscapes or a small number of iFlows. Otherwise, the standard approach is Cloud Transport Management with Content Assembly Service.

Summary

These services work well together. Only two small gaps had to be bridged: an additional zip command for the repository structure, and a wrapper command that extracts the externalized parameters from the Alert Notification event. With those, a single run of the CI/CD job transports an iFlow and sets its environment-specific parameters.

If I understood right, the step you are missing is only to get the file from your PC to the application server, so the standard report can read it there. For that you don't need LSMW or LTMOM: transaction CG3Z ("Upload file") copies a file from the PC to the application server, and CG3Y does the way back.

It is an old EHS transaction, so I checked in an S/4HANA 2023 system that it is still there. It is: CG3Z runs report RC1TCG3Z, which calls function module C13Z_FRONT_END_TO_APPL. Three things you will probably meet:

  • A popup the first time, asking you to read SAP Note 1949906 before you use CG3Y or CG3Z. I couldn't open the note from here, so I don't know what it says. Please read it first.
  • Authorization: before it writes, C13Z_FILE_UPLOAD_BINARY (and the ASCII one) calls AUTHORITY_CHECK_DATASET with activity write. So you need S_DATASET for writing that file (and S_PATH, if the folder is protected in table SPTH).
  • The target folder is checked. FILE_VALIDATE_NAME compares your target name with the logical file name EHS_FTAPPL_2. In my system its logical path EHS_FTAPPL_PATH_2 has one entry, for UNIX: <P=DIR_TRANS>/<FILENAME>. So on a Linux server the file can only go to the transport directory (or a folder below it) by default. If the standard report reads from another folder, the path is maintained in transaction FILE, usually a job for Basis.

The transfer format starts as BIN. With ASC the code takes the text upload (C13Z_FILE_UPLOAD_ASCII) instead. After the upload you can see the file in AL11.

I only read the code and the FILE entries in S/4HANA 2023. I didn't run CG3Z with a real file, and your system may have other entries in FILE.

entry.title: Re: Cross-company stock transfer: Changed Condition P101...
entry.content:
The fact that Price Source = A (Purchase Order) indicates that P101 is indeed derived from the STO/PO pricing logic. However, the observed behavior suggests that SAP is not re-reading the current PO condition record during billing creation.

Since the billing pricing analysis says "Condition value has been taken from preceding document", the most likely explanation is that the PO pricing data used for intercompany billing was already determined and stored at an earlier stage of the process (for example during delivery creation or PGI processing), and billing simply copies that already-determined value.

Therefore, the key question is not where the price comes from, but at which point in the document flow SAP reads and freezes the PO price.

To verify this, I would suggest:

  • Create an STO with P101 = X.
  • Post PGI.
  • Change P101 in the STO to Y.
  • Create the intercompany billing document.

If billing still shows X, then the price was effectively fixed before billing creation, despite the price source being the PO.

I would also recommend checking whether there are any exits or custom code in the intercompany billing creation process that populate P101. If the business requirement is to always pick up the latest STO price after PGI, standard behavior may need to be enhanced, as SAP appears to be using pricing data determined earlier in the process rather than re-reading the PO at billing creation time.

Additionally, verify the GST tax procedure requirements and tax code GI configuration in FTXP to ensure that interstate transactions suppress JICG/JISG and determine only JIIG based on the vendor region and plant region combination.

From the screenshots, my primary suspicion is that table 003 (Tax Classification) is still providing valid JICG/JISG records for tax code GI, which is why the conditions continue to be determined despite the deletion indicators on other accesses

entry.title: Re: Supplier Confirmation and Price Changes in SAP S/4HANA
entry.content:
For standard SAP S/4HANA Purchase Order Confirmations (Confirmation Category AB), the behavior is generally as follows:

1. Which changes are stored in the supplier confirmation record?

The supplier confirmation stores information related to the supplier's commitment, primarily:

  • Confirmed delivery date
  • Confirmed quantity
  • Confirmation category (AB)
  • Confirmation reference details

The confirmation data is stored as a confirmation schedule linked to the PO item. It represents what the supplier has confirmed, which may differ from the PO.

2. Does a supplier confirmation automatically update the PO?

No, not in standard SAP.

Supplier confirmations do not automatically change:

  • PO delivery date (EKET)
  • PO quantity
  • PO price (conditions)

Instead:

  • The original PO remains unchanged.
  • The confirmed date and quantity are held separately in the confirmation data.
  • MRP, availability calculations, and monitoring transactions can consider the confirmed schedule depending on configuration.

The buyer must manually process a PO change if the supplier's proposal should become the new PO commitment.

3. What happens if the supplier proposes a different price?

In standard SAP:

  • The supplier confirmation (AB confirmation) is not intended to carry pricing information.
  • Price changes are generally not stored in the confirmation record.
  • The PO price is not automatically updated from a supplier confirmation.
  • If confirmations arrive via EDI, SAP can perform message validation and discrepancy checks, but the PO conditions are not automatically overwritten by standard AB confirmation processing.

Therefore, if a supplier proposes:

New delivery date → can be reflected in confirmation.
New quantity → can be reflected in confirmation.
New price → typically requires a separate commercial agreement and a PO change process (ME22N or automated custom process).

entry.title: Re: planning calendar at supplier level
entry.content:
In standard S/4HANA (including embedded PP/DS), supplier calendars maintained in BP are not used by MRP to schedule external procurement proposals. The only standard calendar-based workaround is the MRP planning calendar with periodic lot sizing, which is material-specific and therefore unsuitable for most multi-source procurement scenarios.

Recommended workaround

  • For a true multi-source scenario, standard options are limited:
  • Temporarily adjust vendor-specific planned delivery times before known shutdown periods.
  • Apply manual planning intervention during supplier shutdowns.
  • Implement a custom enhancement/BAdI if supplier-specific calendars must influence MRP dates.
  • Evaluate specialized solutions such as Multi-Planning Calendar (MPC), which provides supplier-specific planning calendar logic, but this is an additional solution and not standard S/4HANA functionality

entry.title: Re: Query on Standard SAP Solution/Tool for RE-FX Contrac...
entry.content:
Hi,

I looked at this in an S/4HANA 2023 system. I didn't find a standard function that moves a RE-FX contract to another company code or changes its contract type, and the BAPI shows why: in BAPI_RE_CN_CHANGE the company code (COMP_CODE), the contract number and the contract type (CONTRACT_TYPE) come only in the key structure BAPI_RE_CONTRACT_KEY. The change structure BAPI_RE_CONTRACT_DATX has no field for the contract's own company code or type (it covers the text, the dates, authorization group, tenancy law, main contract, currency and a few more). So both of your cases, another company code and another contract type in the same company code, end up as new contracts, and the old ones are ended.

The standard pieces for that, all in the system:

  • List and extract: BAPI_RE_CN_GET_LIST (selects by company code and contract type, among others) and BAPI_RE_CN_GET_DETAIL (terms, conditions, partners, object relations, measurements and status).
  • Load: BAPI_RE_CN_CREATE, or the Migration Cockpit object SIF_RE_CONTR_2 "Real estate contract". In my system the older SIF_RE_CONTRACT is marked deprecated, so I would not start with that one.
  • Keep the link: the contract has the field OLD_CONTRACT_NUMBER (RECNTXTOLD in table VICNCN). If you fill it with the source contract number, you can always find the old contract from the new one.

With 5,000 to 60,000 contracts, a test run with a few contracts of each contract type first will show you what the target company code still misses in configuration.

I only read the BAPI code and the Migration Cockpit objects in S/4HANA 2023. I didn't run a transfer, so I can't tell you how postings and open items of the old contracts behave after you end them.

entry.title: Stay Current with SAP SuccessFactors Talent Intelligence Hub: 2H 2026 Updates
entry.content:
Hello SAP SuccessFactors Community!

The 2H 2026 release is here, bringing 14 updates to Talent Intelligence Hub, from new Growth Portfolio capabilities and certificate management to skills governance, data sources and two key deprecations. Let's walk through what has changed.

Talent Intelligence Hub

1. Minor Visual Changes in 2H 2026 

Two text changes are worth noting:

  • Certificates in the Growth Portfolio that are awaiting reviewer approval and not yet added now show a Validity Status of Not Applicable instead of Not Yet Active.
  • On the Manage Data Sources page, partner data sources are now added to the main page with the Add from list button instead of Add.

2. New To-Do Categories for Growth Portfolio Cards on the Home Page 

Two new To-Do categories now appear on the Home page for Growth Portfolio tasks:

  • Proficiency Level Change Requests: shown when an employee changes a proficiency level on an attribute that has an approval workflow. The card shows the employee, attribute type, requested level and previous level.
  • Certificate Change Requests: the card shows the employee, certificate name, issue date and submission date.

SAP recommends completing all pending To-Do tasks before using the new categories, as older tasks may show actions that are no longer applicable.

3. REST API for Growth Portfolio Export 

A new REST API exports employee skills data from the Growth Portfolio for reporting, analysis and other downstream uses, complementing the export options in Integration Center. 

  • Included: active and inactive skill records for active and inactive users, and current proficiency levels.
  • Not included: recommended skills not yet added, and historical proficiency levels.

Only authorized users and partner data sources can access the data through this API.

4. New Sorting and Filtering Option to Export Attributes 

The updated Talent Intelligence Hub Attribute Export Integration Center Definition (.icd) file from the SAP Business Accelerator Hub adds advanced filtering and sorting. For example, you can export skills and exclude competencies, and order the output as you prefer. Time-based filters are not supported yet and do not affect results. SAP recommends moving to the updated file, as the existing template will no longer be supported from 1H 2027.

5. Enhancements to Skills Governance and Standardization 

Skills in the Attributes Library, including those pending administrator review on the Skills Governance page, are now automatically scanned and mapped to their SAP Taxonomy names.

  • Skills landing page: Taxonomy Mapping and SAP Taxonomy Name replace Standardization Status as filters and columns, and the Skills Governance button shows the count of skills awaiting review.
  • Creating a skill: the Proposed Name and Standardization Status fields become SAP Taxonomy Name and Taxonomy Mapping. The options are Taxonomy name and mapping (renamed to the SAP name, included in AI recommendations, translations inherited), Entered name and mapping (keeps your name, included in AI recommendations, translations maintained manually) and No mapping (custom skill, excluded from AI recommendations, translations maintained manually).
  • Publishing from the Imported tab: Taxonomy Mapping is now chosen per skill in the Publish dialog, and each option shows the resulting skill name.
  • Inferred Skills tab: a new Inference Details tab shows the inferred count and confidence score for a skill.

6. Employee Defined Validity for Certificates 

Certificates can now be set to User Defined validity. The system then stops calculating the expiry date from the issue date and duration, and employees pick the Expiry Date themselves with a date picker when adding the certificate to their Growth Portfolio. That date drives expiry notifications and expiring soon indicators, which suits certificates with non-standard validity periods.

7. Enhancements to Data Sources 

Besides partner integrations, custom data sources can now be created on the Manage Data Sources page with a name, code and optional description. The code is automatically prefixed with CUST_, and the source is Inactive until activated.

  • Rating Overwrite Allowed and Rating Lowering Allowed default to No for custom data sources.
  • Trusted Data Source defaults to No, so skills governance applies. Setting it to Yes bypasses governance.
  • When skills from a custom data source are imported, its name appears in the skill's Timeline.

8. Deprecation of Center of Capabilities 

Center of Capabilities reaches End of Development and End of Maintenance on November 13, 2026, and will be deleted on May 12, 2028. SAP recommends migrating to Talent Intelligence Hub by 2H 2027 to manage competency data.

Action: Required. Future dates are subject to change.

9. New Archive Option for Skills in Growth Portfolio 

Employees can archive non-role-based skills that no longer match their role or development goals, without permanently removing them. Archived skills move to a separate Archived tab and are excluded from active learning recommendations and opportunities, but stay available in historical searches for succession and recruiting. They can be reactivated or removed, and activity recorded from other sources does not change them. Archiving applies only to skills, not other attribute types.

10. Enhanced Flow for Removal of Attributes in Growth Portfolio 

Attributes an employee removes now move to an Inactive tab for their attribute type. They are read-only, and their opportunity recommendations and development goals are no longer shown. Certificates do not support Remove yet.

  • An employee can add an inactive attribute back from its details page or the attribute picker.
  • Completing a linked activity elsewhere, such as an Opportunity Marketplace assignment or a Learning course, reactivates it automatically.
  • If an administrator sets the attribute to inactive in Talent Intelligence Hub, it disappears from the tab and returns once reactivated. The Timeline logs inactivation and reactivation as separate entries.

11. Enhancements to Certificates in Growth Portfolio 

Several changes simplify certificate management:

  • Acquired tab: certificates the employee has added, split into Critical for Role, Non-Critical for Role and Others (added independently, not tied to the role).
  • Missing tab: role-related certificates not yet added, split into Critical for Role and Non-Critical for Role.
  • Withdraw: employees can withdraw a certificate that is pending reviewer approval or sent back for corrections.
  • Action Required filter: shows certificates to Renew, Resubmit (sent back by reviewers) or Add Critical (critical for the role, not yet added).

12. Role-Based Skill Classification in Job Profile 

A new Requirement Level field on the Manage Job Profile Content page marks each skill mapped to a job role as Mandatory (core to the role) or Optional (relevant but not strictly required). Employees in the role then see these skills in their Growth Portfolio tagged as Critical for Role or Non-Critical for Role, helping them tell essential skills from complementary ones.

13. Support for Mapping Certificates with Job Roles 

A new Mapped Certificates tab on the Manage Job Profile Content page lets administrators map Talent Intelligence Hub certificates to job roles in Job Profile Builder. The Critical toggle marks a certificate as essential for the role. Mapped certificates appear for employees in the role under Missing, as Critical for Role or Non-Critical for Role, and can be added directly from there.

14. Deprecation of Job Description Manager 

Job Description Manager, the framework for managing legacy job families and roles, reached End of Development and End of Maintenance on May 15, 2026, and will be deleted on November 12, 2027. SAP recommends moving to Job Profile Builder and Talent Intelligence Hub to manage job families, job roles, skills and other attributes.

Action: Required. Future dates are subject to change.

That wraps up the 2H 2026 Talent Intelligence Hub updates. Do refer to the SAP Help Portal and What's New Viewer for the latest details, and let me know in the comments which update you are most looking forward to.

entry.title: Managing Multiple Company Codes with SAP Document AI
entry.content:
Large enterprises rarely process documents in a single legal entity. Accounts payable teams handle supplier invoices across dozens of company codes. HR shared services process onboarding documents for employees across multiple subsidiaries. Quality management teams receive certificates and inspection reports addressed to different plants. Procurement teams handle order confirmations sent to different buying entities.

In all of these scenarios, the same challenge comes up early: how do you configure SAP Document AI to handle multiple company codes or legal entities cleanly? The document type is the same across entities. The fields you want to extract are the same. But the legal entity matters for routing, authorization, and downstream ERP posting.

This post walks through a clean architecture for managing multiple company codes in SAP Document AI, and then goes further by using the workflow engine to inject organizational context that the document itself cannot provide.

The configuration steps in this post are based on the SAP Document AI Workspace UI.

The Architecture: One Schema, Context Injected by the Channel

SAP Document AI separates where a document comes from (the inbound channel) from how it is processed (the schema and workflow). That separation is the foundation of a clean multi-entity setup.

Here is what it looks like:

One schema per document type. Add company code as an input field in the schema. Input fields have their value injected at upload time, never extracted from the document. They can also be set to hidden so they do not appear in the reviewer UI at all, keeping the review screen clean while still carrying the value for routing and downstream processing.

One inbound channel per company code. This assumes each company code has a dedicated inbound mailbox or monitored folder. If that is already in place, each channel maps cleanly to one legal entity and becomes the authoritative source of the organizational context.

Company code injected as an input entity at upload time. Each channel is configured with a fixed input value: 1010 for one channel, 2020 for another. The value is set once per channel and injected automatically on every document that arrives. This is not extracted from the document content. It is asserted by the intake channel, which is the authoritative source.

Authorization separation via AMS restriction policies. In the Identity Authentication Service (IAS), restriction policies scope document visibility to the input entity value. Users in the 1010 team are scoped to documents carrying companyCode = 1010. The separation is enforced at the platform level, not by keeping schemas in separate buckets.

As the organization grows, onboarding a new company code means adding a channel with its fixed value.

How to Configure It

Step 1: Define the input field in your schema

In Schema UI, add a field for company code (or plant code, subsidiary, or whichever organizational identifier you need). Set the field type to String and place it in the appropriate group.

Once added, open Edit Settings for the field. There are four settings to configure:

  • Processor Type: Input — the value is injected at upload time, not read from the document.
  • Mandatory: Yes — ensures the field cannot be empty. The channel must always supply a value.
  • Read Only: Yes — prevents reviewers from overwriting the injected value in the UI.
  • Hide in Prediction: Yes — hides the field from the reviewer screen entirely; it carries its value silently for downstream use.
  • Authorization Relevant: Yes — marks this field as the basis for document-level access control via IAS restriction policies.


All five settings configured for a company code input field.

Click Save, then Activate the schema version.

Step 2: Set the fixed value per channel

In the channel configuration, go to step 4 (Input Parameter). You will see all input fields from the schema listed. Enter the fixed value for this channel: e.g. 1010 for one company code, 2020 for another. Same schema, different value per channel.

Step 3: Repeat per channel

Create one channel per company code. Each channel gets its own fixed input value. The schema and workflow stay unchanged.

Step 4: Configure authorization in IAS

In the Identity Authentication Service, define restriction policies that scope document visibility to the input entity value. Users assigned to the 1010 AP team receive a policy that limits their document access to documents carrying companyCode = 1010. This replaces the authorization separation that would otherwise require separate schemas or separate tenants.

Going Further: Injecting Plant Code from the Sender Address

A dedicated channel per company code works well when email routing is already in place. But some organizational context cannot be resolved from the channel alone. A condition node in the workflow can inspect the sender address and inject additional values as input entities.

SAP.EmailUtils.getFrom(fileId).getAddress()

A condition node branches on this value:

  • If sender is supplier-a@acme.com or supplier-b@acme.com: set plantCode = "0001" as input entity
  • If sender is supplier-c@acme.com: set plantCode = "0002" as input entity
  • Default: leave plantCode empty, route to manual review

This works because the sender-to-plant mapping is a business rule your organization might already maintain. 

Putting It Together: The Multi-Entity Workflow

A production-grade multi-entity workflow combining these patterns looks like this:

  1. Document arrives via entity-specific inbound channel. Channel injects companyCode as input entity.
  2. Email Split node separates body and attachments.
  3. For-Each loop iterates over relevant attachments.
  4. Sender address condition: match sender against known supplier-to-plant mappings. Inject plantCode, costCenter, or subsidiary as input entity.
  5. Extraction node: runs against the shared schema. By the time extraction runs, the organizational context is already in the document. SAP Document AI extracts what only the document can provide: numbers, dates, line items, amounts, names.
  6. Confidence condition: route to auto-confirm or review queue.
  7. Outbound notification: deliver to SAP Integration Suite or downstream system with a fully enriched document.

What You Gain

This architecture gives you:

  • One schema to maintain regardless of how many legal entities, plants, or subsidiaries you onboard
  • Higher data quality on organizational fields because they come from controlled, authoritative sources rather than OCR interpretation
  • Authorization enforced at the platform level via IAS restriction policies, not by structural separation of schemas or tenants

entry.title: Re: AIF IDoc Outbound Processing, no message for IDoc sen...
entry.content:
Hi,

I followed this in the AIF code of an S/4HANA 2023 system. I can't tell you yet why your first entry is empty, but the code shows where to look, and there is a hook for your third question.

Who writes status 18: the port function /AIF/SINGLE_IDOC_PORT_FUNCTION (function group /AIF/IDOC_OUTBOUND). It hands the IDoc to AIF (/AIF/CL_ENABLER_IDOC=>TRANSFER_TO_AIF), runs /AIF/FILE_PROCESS_DATA with your mapping and actions, and on success writes status 18 with message /AIF/IDOC 003, the "IDoc processed successfully by SAP Application Interface Framework" you see in WE05. No line of that function fills APPL_LOG in the status record.

What the first entry shows depends on the logging engine of its interface (field LOG_ENGINE_ID in /AIF/T_FINF, the classes are in /AIF/S_ENGINES):

  • 001 = /AIF/CL_LOGGING_ENGINE_IDOCSTA. It keeps no messages of its own: ADD_MESSAGES and ADD_BAL_MESSAGES are empty, with the comment "no implementation needed, since in this case no application log exists". The log is rebuilt from the IDoc status records, and when the last one is /AIF/IDOC 003 or 004, only that one is shown.
  • 000 = /AIF/CL_LOGGING_ENGINE_APP_LOG, the AIF application log.

For the hook: TRANSFER_TO_AIF calls a customer function module ZAIF_IDOC_ON_SEND if it exists (checked with FUNCTION_EXISTS, the code refers to notes 1922367 and 1958537). It gets namespace, interface, version and the status records, and can change the log messages (CT_LOG_MESSAGES) and the message status before the enabler stores the entry. With engine 001 I would not expect a message added there to survive, because of the empty ADD_MESSAGES above. I didn't read the APP_LOG engine for that.

So my question back: which LOG_ENGINE_ID does the interface of your first entry have? With 001, by the code above, I would expect to see the 003 message there, so an empty log would point to something else, maybe a message type filter in /AIF/ERR.

I only read the code in S/4HANA 2023. My system has no IDoc processed this way, so nothing of this was run.

entry.title: SAP BASIS HEALTH CHECK COCKPIT – ONE ABAP REPORT (NO SOLMAN / NO CALM)
entry.content:
Hello everyone,

It has been a long time since my last blog post. Work kept me busy, and honestly I only wanted to come back with something new, something that's not already on the community and that can really save time for others. I don't like repetitive work, and I don't like writing about things that already have ten blog posts. So here I am with a new one.

All my earlier blog posts were on Basis technical topics. This is my first blog post with ABAP . As a Basis person I'm not a full-time developer, but this need came straight from my daily work, so I decided to build it myself.

In this blog post we will learn:

  • How a Basis team can do active daily monitoring without SAP Solution Manager, SAP Cloud ALM or any other monitoring tool
  • How one ABAP report checks around 28 areas (application server, HANA DB, security, transport, interfaces and mail) in one run
  • How red / yellow / green colors help you see problems straight away
  • The prerequisites (2 Z-tables plus indexes) and the full source code, ready to copy

Here is the trailer, for full picture scroll down 🙃

THE PROBLEM – WHY I BUILT THIS:

Many landscapes, especially small and mid-size customers, do not have SolMan or CALM connected. Sometimes it's licence, sometimes the project is "still planned", sometimes nobody owns it. But the business still expects the Basis team to know about a problem before users call.

So what do we do? Every morning we open the same transactions, one by one:

SM51 → SM50 → SM66 → ST22 → SM37 → SM13 → SM12 → SP01 → SMLG → ST06 → DBACOCKPIT → STRUST → SCC4 → SE06 → STMS → SM58 → SMQ1 → SMQ2 → SOST …

and then the same again for the next system.

In my experience this takes [30–45] minutes per system if everything is fine, and more if something is not. After some days the eyes get used to the screens and small things get missed: one cancelled job, one SYSFAIL queue, a certificate expiring in 25 days. That is exactly what comes back later as a P1 ticket.

I wanted one screen that tells me what's wrong, how bad it is, and where to click to fix it.

WHAT THE REPORT DOES:

The report is ZBC_HEALTH_COCKPIT. In simple words:

  1. You pick a time window (since last run, today, yesterday, last N hours or a date/time range).
  2. The report runs all selected checks and gives each finding a severity.
  3. You get a summary ALV, one row per check, with the worst issues on top.
  4. Double-click a row → detail ALV with every finding for that check.
  5. Double-click a detail row → it jumps straight to the transaction (SM37, ST22, SMQ2, STRUST …), with authority check.
  6. Results are saved to history, and old runs are deleted automatically after N days (minimum 7).

SEVERITY AND COLOURS:

Severity Color Meaning
CRITICAL 🔴 RedAct now
HIGH🟠 OrangeAct today
WARNING🟡 YellowKeep an eye on it
INFO 🔵 BlueInformation only
OK🟢 GreenAll good
NOT CHECKED ⚪ GreyCheck could not run (authorization, connection…). Never shown as green.

That last point matters to me. If a check fails, it should never look green. A false green is worse than no monitoring at all.

CHECKS COVERED:

Area Checks
Application serverSM51 servers up/ping, SM50 free DIA/BTC/UPD WPs %, SM66 long-running WPs, ST22 dumps (with top runtime errors), SM37 cancelled jobs, SM13 update errors, SM12 old locks, spool number range %, SMLG logon group reachability/response, ST06 OS CPU / RAM / swap / disk I/O
Database (SAP HANA)Current and historical HANA alerts, data/log backup age (log_mode aware), memory vs allocation limit, CPU, disk volumes, services
Security & transportSSL certificate expiry (via standard report SSF_ALERT_CERTEXPIRE), SCC4 client open/closed, SE06 system/namespace change option, STMS imports with RC 4 / RC 8+
Interfaces & mailSM58 tRFC errors, SMQ1 / SMQ2 queues in error/stop, SOST failed/waiting mails

Every threshold (Warn / High / Critical) can be set on the selection screen, so you can save one variant for PRD and a different one for QAS/DEV.

1st screen of the report: where pre-select data will be there and also can be change based on your requirement keep last run reason as we have table too to store the data so not need to worry much but based on requirement you can select the options.

as there are multiple screens, every area param can be selected from each tab.

every tab have options, where you can change or update the values based on requirement and save it as variant, coz every landscape is having different requirement so instead of static i kept it dynamic so no code change needed only screen value is sufficient.

once executed it will show the top level ALV, where we can doubleclick on line item to see the details, if click on tcode it will route you tcode screen also

and in detail while click on that line item it will be easy to navigate and show the error information like below for each

every section and its details, a ease of life for monitoring team 😎

HOW THIS HELPS IN DAILY LIFE:

  • Time saving: my morning check went from [30–45] minutes to about [2–5] minutes per system. Run it, look at the red and orange rows, double-click, fix.
  • Better eye attention: we humans spot red much faster than a number in a column. Problems jump out of the screen.
  • Nothing gets skipped: on a busy day it's tempting to skip "just SOST" or "just STRUST". The report never skips.
  • Background job friendly: schedule it in SM36 with a variant (e.g. every 2–4 hours). With "Since last successful run" each run only looks at what's new since the previous one, so there's no overlap and no gap.
  • History for audits and handover: results stay in Z-tables, so you can show "what was the system status last Tuesday at 08:00".
  • Same standard for the whole team: a junior colleague and a senior colleague look at the same checks and the same thresholds.

A monitoring report can't be tested properly on a blank sandbox; you need real dumps, real jobs, a real HANA. Thank you, my friend, for the trust and the support. 🙏

entry.title: Re: SAP BTP ABAP Trial: HTTP 401 when requesting ADT reen...
entry.content:
Hi,

A 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm and sap-authenticated: false does not, by itself, mean that your user is missing authorizations. I measured the logon flow of a BTP ABAP environment step by step (an SAP Learning practice system, not the trial, so check if yours looks the same), and that exact answer is what the API host gives to any request that arrives without a session or a ticket. Three read-only checks:

  1. Open https://<your-instance-host>/sap/public/bc/icf/virtualhost. It is public and returns two hosts: API (https://<guid>.abap.<region>.hana.ondemand.com) and UI (https://<guid>.abap-web.<region>.hana.ondemand.com/ui).
  2. Compare with the host your 401 came from. In my test, the .abap. host answered requests without a ticket with 401 and the Basic realm of system and client, like yours. The .abap-web. host is the one that redirects you to the logon of the identity provider. So a browser request straight to the .abap. host ends in this 401 unless it carries a ticket or a token.
  3. Log on through the UI host (the /ui page you already reach) and see if the launchpad opens after the logon. If it does, user and identity provider are fine, and I would look at the ADT side next, starting with the host in the project. If the logon itself fails there, it points to the user or the trial access, before any ABAP authorization.

For the ticket itself, the browser flow that worked for me was <UI>/sap/bc/sec/reentrance?scenario=FTO1&redirect-url=http://localhost:<port>/..., which came back with a reentrance-ticket parameter. With that ticket in the header MYSAPSSO2 (plus x-sap-security-session: create), the API host opened a session. I didn't call /sap/bc/adt/core/http/reentranceticket in that test, so I can't say more about that exact endpoint.

None of these steps changes anything in your instance.

entry.title: Solution order billing with solution bundle
entry.content:
Introduction

When selling bundled solutions — a set of products and services packaged together – sometimes solution bundles are sold with an aggregated price and individual subitems are not priced separately for the end customer. Sometimes it could be that the solution bundle is sold without providing information about the subitems.  There could be other scenarios too. The billing document should also keep the information displayed consistent to the selling and show the structure in the same way.

Solution Order in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition natively supports solution bundles, where a main bundle product contains multiple sub-items — subscription products, professional services, and support contracts. However, to surface this bundle hierarchy on the billing document, a few configuration and extensibility steps are required.

This blog walks you through an approach to achieve that.

Solution Bundle

You will find more information about the solution bundle topic in the following places:

  • Blog: Advanced-solution-bundling-for-solution-order-management-in-sap-s-4hana
  • SAP Help: Bundle Items in Solution Orders

 

Example of billing document with solution bundle

The sample billing document is the example we use in this blog. Each bundle appears as a main line item, with its sub-items grouped and indented beneath it — giving the customer a clear, structured view of what they are being billed for. Note that here we do not want to show the net value for the subitems.

Achieving this output requires a couple of custom fields, BAdI logic, form template enhancement and a couple of configuration settings to be set up.

Configuration Overview

#

Step

1

Create custom fields on the Billing Document Item

2

Create BAdI implementation to populate the custom fields

3

Assign the BAdI implementation to billing document creation process

4

Configure addition of Solution Bundle in Margin Analysis (if needed)

5

Enable generation of a single bill for Solution Order

6

Configure grouping by Solution Bundle for Output

7

Create custom form for adjusting aggregation for Solution Bundle in Output

 

Step 1: Create custom fields on the Billing Document Item

The billing document item must be extended with three custom fields to carry bundle metadata from the originating solution order.

App: Custom Fields and Logic (F1481)

Custom Logic app or Custom Logic tab within Custom Fields and Logic app

Create the following three fields. For each, set Business Context = Billing: Billing Document Item.

Field Technical Name

Label

Type

YY1_BUNDLEITEMNUM_BDI

Bundle Item Number

Text (6)

YY1_BUNDLEPRODID_BDI

Bundle Product ID

Text (40)

YY1_BUNDLEPRODDESC_BDI

Bundle Product Description

Text (40)

 

For each field, before publishing:

1.1  In the UIs and Reports tab, enable the form template SDBIL_CI_PROF_SRV_XX. (XX denotes the language key DE, EN …)

1.2  Save and Publish.

These three fields form the foundation for everything that follows. They will hold the bundle product ID, the bundle item number, and the bundle product description at the billing item level.

Step 2: Create BAdI implementation to populate the custom fields

The custom fields need to be filled automatically whenever a billing document is created from a solution order. This is handled through a BAdI (Business Add-In).

App: Custom Fields and Logic (F1481) → Custom Logic tab

  • Business Context: Sales: Billing Document Item
  • BAdI Description: Custom Data Transfer for Billing Documents(SD_BIL_DATA_TRANSFER)
  • Implementation Description: Fill Bundle Details & Control SO Invoice Split

 

The BAdI implementation does two things:

2.1  Populates the custom fields representing solution bundle info — for each billing item originating from a solution order, it reads BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct and BusSolnOrdItemBundleItem from the CDS view I_BusSolutionOrderItemEnhcd, then fetches the product description from I_ProductText. These values are written into the three YY1_ fields on the billing item. These fields are used in the custom form for print.

2.2  Controls the invoice split — it clears documentreferenceid and purchaseorderbycustomer at the header level when solution order items are present, ensuring bundle items are consolidated onto a single billing document rather than split.

   ```abap

    MOVE-CORRESPONDING bil_doc TO bil_doc_res.

    MOVE-CORRESPONDING bil_doc_item TO bil_doc_item_res.

    MOVE-CORRESPONDING bil_doc_item_contr TO bil_doc_item_contr_res.

 

    READ TABLE bil_doc_item TRANSPORTING NO FIELDS WITH KEY businesssolutionorder IS NOT INITIAL.

    IF sy-subrc = 0.

      CLEAR bil_doc_res-documentreferenceid.

      CLEAR bil_doc_res-purchaseorderbycustomer.

    ENDIF.

 

    LOOP AT bil_doc_item_res ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_item_res>).

      READ TABLE bil_doc_item ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_item_orig>) WITH KEY billingdocumentitem = <fs_item_res>-billingdocumentitem.

      IF sy-subrc <> 0. CONTINUE. ENDIF.

 

      SELECT SINGLE BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct, BusSolnOrdItemBundleItem

        FROM I_BusSolutionOrderItemEnhcd

        WHERE BusinessSolutionOrder = @<fs_item_orig>-businesssolutionorder

          AND BusinessSolutionOrderItem = @<fs_item_orig>-businesssolutionorderitem

        INTO @DATA(ls_bundle_info).

 

      IF sy-subrc = 0.

        <fs_item_res>-yy1_bundleprodid_bdi    = ls_bundle_info-BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct.

        <fs_item_res>-yy1_bundleitemnum_bdi   = ls_bundle_info-BusSolnOrdItemBundleItem.

 

        SELECT SINGLE ProductDescription FROM I_ProductText

          WHERE Product = @LS_bundle_info-BusSolnOrdItemBundleProduct AND Language = @SY-langu

          INTO @<fs_item_res>-yy1_bundleproddesc_bdi.

      ENDIF.

    ENDLOOP.

    ```

Make a note of the Implementation ID generated (e.g., YY1_SOMEBADIIMPLEMENTATIONID) — it is needed in the next step. Publish the logic after saving.

Step 3: Assign the BAdI implementation to billing document creation process

The BAdI from Step 2 must be triggered every time a billing document is created. This is done by defining a custom copy routine and assigning it in copy control.

3.1  Define the Custom Routine

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUI 102865 (Define Custom Data Transfer Routines for Billing Documents)

3.1.1  Create a New Entry.

3.1.2  Enter a Routine Number from the custom range, e.g., 3000001.

3.1.3  Enter the BAdI Implementation ID from Step 2.

3.1.4  Save.

3.2  Assign the Routine in Copy Control

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUIs 102762,102763 and 102764 for copy controls for billing documents

3.2.1  Open the relevant copy control relationship (e.g., Delivery Document  to Billing Document or Billing to Billing).

3.2.2  Navigate to the Item level.

3.2.3  For each relevant Item Category, locate the field `Custom data Transfer `.

3.2.4  Replace the existing routine number with your new custom routine number (e.g., 3000001).

3.2.5  Save.

From this point on, every billing document created for items with the assigned category will execute the BAdI and populate the solution bundle fields.

Step 4: Configure addition of Solution Bundle in Margin Analysis

If you want to also report on the solution bundle then you can enable the custom fields created for accounting too:

4.1  In the Business Scenarios tab for each of the custom fields, enable Sales: Billing Document to Accounting: Journal Entry Integration. Save and publish.

4.2  Follow the blog Enable-profitability-reporting-for-bundle-in-solution-order-management for the custom fields.

Step 5: Enable generation of a single bill for Solution Order

Make use of blog Collective-billing-of-solution-order-include-prof-serv-project-and-other-docs-into-single-invoice to bring together all billing items from solution order and the solution bundle together on a single invoice, if you have a customer project in the solution order or the solution bundle.

Step 6: Configure grouping by Solution Bundle for Output

The billing output form must be enhanced to include the custom bundle fields so they appear on the printed or PDF document. Here, the form template for professional services billing document is reused. With this, the aggregate rule configuration for grouping was used.  This makes it possible to group the items by bundle product and bundle item without modifications required for the form.

There may be an alternative approach with the standard billing document template too that you may want to explore.

6.1  Configure Flexible Billing Output Aggregation

This is the step that produces the hierarchical display in the billing output — grouping sub-items visually beneath their parent bundle, exactly as shown in the sample invoice.

6.2  Define the Aggregation Rule

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUI 103967 (Define Rules for Flexible Billing Output Aggregation – PS)

Create a Rule with the following Group Items aggregation levels(eg 9):

Level

Field

Level 1

YY1_BUNDLEITEMNUM_BDI

Level 2

YY1_BUNDLEPRODDESC_BDI

 

6.3  Define the Formula (Trigger Condition)

App: Manage Your Solution → SSCUI 104023 (Define Formulas for Flexible Billing Output Aggregation – PS)

6.3.1 Create a formula and assign Set Aggregation Rule to 9

6.3.2 Create an entry in the Define Decision Table and add the Aggregation Rule 9

With this in place, the output form will automatically group billing items by bundle and present them hierarchically on the output document.

Step 7: Create custom form for adjusting aggregation for Solution Bundle in Output

This step to modify the form template is needed because the output example we have in this blog, should show the subitems of the bundle but not their prices. If prices of the subitems are to be displayed and only aggregation is required then this step would not be required. With step 6 execution, that would be achieved.

7.1  Download the form template to modify for use

App: Maintain Form Templates (F1434)

7.1.1  Download the standard template: SDBIL_CI_PROF_SRV_XX.

7.1.2  Open the .xdp file in Adobe LiveCycle Designer.

7.1.3  In the Data View, the three custom fields — YY1_BUNDLEITEMNUM_BDI, YY1_BUNDLEPRODID_BDI, YY1_BUNDLEPRODDESC_BDI — should be available for each item. Use them to enhance the item table in the form layout to aggregate by solution bundle but hide the prices of the subitems.

7.1.4  Save the modified file with a new name, e.g., Z_PROF_SRV_FORM_BUNDLE.xdp.

7.2  Upload the custom form and define output rules

App: Maintain Form Templates (F1434)

7.2.1  Upload Z_PROF_SRV_FORM_BUNDLE.xdp.

 

App: Output Parameter Determination(W0138)

7.2.2  Select Billing Document in Show Rules for and Form Template in Determination Step in Select Business Rules section.

7.2.3  Create an entry and assign the form template Z_PROF_SRV_FORM_BUNDLE to be used by the billing document to be created by solution order in the Maintain Business Rules section.   

 

How this looks in action

You would find the extension fields for the solution bundle in the list of the available fields which you access using the gear icon on the top right corner of the item table on the billing document. You can make them visible for the item table.

You will find the output entry for the billing document has the new form assigned to it. You can use the preview option to view it.

entry.title: Re: How to restrict cross-creation between Customers and...
entry.content:
Hi Aline,

I read the CVI code in my S/4HANA 2023 lab to see what makes the BP create the customer and where the account group authorization is checked. Lakshmipathi's point 3 (F_KNA1_GRP and F_LFA1_GRP) is the one that should stop it. Two details from the code may explain why it depends on the grouping in your system:

  1. The customer comes from the role category, not from the grouping. CVI_KA_BP_CUSTOMER=>IS_BP_IN_CUSTOMER_ROLE reads TBD002 ("Set BP Role Category for Direction BP to Customer") for the role categories of the BP: DEB = X means a customer is required, DEB_FLAG = X means it is optional. The grouping is not used there. It comes in afterwards, for the account group and the number (TBD001, "Define Number Assignment for Direction BP to Customer"). The vendor side is the same with TBC002 and TBC001. In my lab, FLCU00 and FLCU01 are only in TBD002, and FLVN00 and FLVN01 only in TBC002. If a role category that your vendor users may maintain is also in TBD002 (or the other way around), every BP with that role gets a customer, and B_BUPA_RLT can't stop it, because the user is allowed to maintain that role.
  2. F_KNA1_GRP is checked for the customer of the BP, not for the role the user is maintaining. When the BP is going to get a customer, CVI_BDT_ADAPTER_INTERN checks it twice: in the AUTH1 event (GENERIC_AUTH1) and again before saving (GENERIC_DCHCK, with the comment "Check only customer account group authorization"). The fields are KTOKD and ACTVT. For suppliers it checks F_LFA1_GRP (KTOKK, ACTVT) the same way. So a vendor profile without F_KNA1_GRP for 01 and 02 should get an error before saving when CVI wants to create a customer.

One detail that does depend on the grouping: if "Flexible Grouping" is set for the grouping in TBD001 (TBC001 for suppliers), the AUTH1 check turns the F_KNA1_GRP error into a warning on create, because the account group can still be changed in the BP. The check before saving has no such exception, so going by the code the save should still stop.

If a vendor user can still save a BP that gets a customer, I would look at the user's F_KNA1_GRP values in SUIM, for example a copied FI or SD role with KTOKD *.

I only read the code and the customizing tables in my 2023 lab. I didn't create a BP with a restricted user, so please confirm it with an authorization trace (STAUTHTRACE) in your system.
